A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
labor market rigidities are an important source of persistence in current account imbalances.
labor market institutions are an important factor that determines the speed of current account adjustment.
the intertemporal model of current account adjustment, which has been the standard model for decades, needs to be updated to account for domestic labor market rigidities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
domestic labor market institutions play a crucial role in the current account adjustment process.
the current account is not a passive variable in the adjustment to shocks but rather an important mechanism through which an economy adjusts.
the intertemporal trade and intra-temporal trade channels are complementary in the adjustment to a shock.
